topic_ko: 공유된 사회적 이해 — 안락한 방보다 안정된 집단이 먼저다
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 32번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다.

passage: The deepest of our cognitive drives pushes us to make sense of our surroundings so that we can foresee what is coming.
Above all, we want the meanings we build to be held by the people around us as well.
Consider a college that admits more students than its dormitories can hold in a particular year.
Some newcomers are placed in lounges, and others are placed in campus hotel rooms.
The trouble with a lounge is obvious enough, since it offers no closet and little privacy.
Yet a hotel room provides a private bathroom, a personal television and far more space.
Even so, hotel residents suffer, because they belong to no settled circle of neighbors for the year ahead.
They must wait in uncertainty for a social place, lacking the shared understanding a stable group would give them.
choices: why colleges should build more dormitory rooms each year
how physical comfort determines student satisfaction on campus
why privacy has become the main concern of modern students
how a need for shared social understanding shapes what people want
why uncertainty about grades harms academic performance
theme.explanation_ko: 사람들이 원하는 것은 물리적 편의가 아니라 타인과 공유되는 의미, 즉 안정된 집단에서 나오는 공유된 사회적 이해라는 내용이 주제이다. ④가 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①기숙사 증축, ②물리적 편의 결정론, ③사생활, ⑤성적 불안은 본문의 초점이 아니다.

passage: When we judge where students should live, we should stop counting only bathrooms and square meters.
The most basic cognitive drive leads people to make their surroundings predictable.
For that reason, people want meanings that the people around them also hold.
A campus hotel room offers privacy, a personal television and generous space.
A crowded dormitory lounge offers none of these comforts at all.
Yet hotel residents are the ones who wait in uncertainty, with no settled group of neighbors.
What they lack is the shared social understanding that membership in a stable group provides.
Housing decisions should therefore be judged by the stable communities they create, not by amenities alone.
choices: 대학은 신입생 수를 예측해 기숙사 정원을 미리 늘려야 한다.
학생 숙소는 편의 시설이 아니라 안정된 공동체를 만들어 주는지로 평가해야 한다.
사생활 보장이 대학 기숙사 설계의 최우선 기준이 되어야 한다.
학생들은 낯선 환경에서도 스스로 사회적 자리를 찾으려 노력해야 한다.
대학은 호텔을 임시 숙소로 활용하는 관행을 즉시 중단해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 편의 시설을 다 갖춘 호텔이 오히려 문제인 이유가 안정된 집단의 부재이므로, 숙소는 공동체 형성 여부로 평가해야 한다는 주장이다. ②가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①정원 확대, ③사생활 우선, ④개인의 노력, ⑤호텔 사용 중단은 본문 주장과 다르거나 지엽적이다.

passage: Our most basic cognitive motivation drives us to understand our surroundings and predict what will happen.
More than anything, we prefer meanings that other people around us also accept.
When a college admits more students than expected, some end up in lounges and others in campus hotels.
The lounge is clearly inconvenient because it has no closet and no real privacy.
The hotel room, by contrast, offers a private bathroom, a personal television and more space.
Nevertheless, hotel residents belong to no stable group of year-long neighbors.
They wait in uncertainty until they can find a social place of their own.
The uncertainty itself, not the room, is what makes their situation difficult.
choices: 물리적 편의가 충분하면 어떤 거주 환경도 만족스러워진다.
대학은 예상보다 많은 입학생을 받지 않도록 주의해야 한다.
사생활이 보장될수록 사람들의 심리적 안정감은 커진다.
학생들은 새로운 환경에서 빠르게 적응하는 법을 배워야 한다.
사람들은 안정된 집단에서 나오는 공유된 이해를 편의보다 더 필요로 한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 편의를 다 갖춘 호텔이 오히려 문제였던 이유는 안정된 집단에서 나오는 공유된 사회적 이해가 없었기 때문이다. ⑤가 요지.
gist.distractor_ko: ①은 본문이 반박하는 통념이고, ②③④는 글의 결론이 아니다.

passage: The most fundamental cognitive motivation pushes people to make their environment predictable.
Above all, people want the meanings they form to be shared by those around them.
Imagine a year when a college accepts more students than its dormitories can house.
Some students are sent to lounges, while others receive rooms in a campus hotel.
A lounge plainly falls short, offering no closet and almost no privacy.
A hotel room, in contrast, comes with its own bathroom, its own television and extra space.
Still, hotel residents have no settled circle of neighbors for the coming year.
Waiting in uncertainty for a social place turns out to be worse than living without a closet.
choices: Why Campus Hotels Are the Future of Student Housing
The Hidden Cost of Comfort: Living Without a Group
How Colleges Should Predict Their Admission Numbers
Privacy First: Redesigning the Modern Dormitory
Closets, Bathrooms and the Science of Room Design
title.explanation_ko: 편의는 갖췄지만 집단이 없어 치르는 대가를 압축한 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①호텔 예찬, ③입학 예측, ④사생활 중심 설계, ⑤방 설계 과학은 글의 초점이 아니다.

passage: Our deepest cognitive drive is to understand our surroundings well enough to predict them.
For that reason people prefer meanings that others around them hold as well.
When a college over-enrolls, some students live in lounges and others in campus hotels.
The lounge is obviously uncomfortable, lacking even a closet.
The hotel room offers a private bathroom, a personal television and generous space.
Yet the hotel students are the ones still waiting to learn where they belong.
A comfortable room with no neighbors is a well-furnished waiting area.
What they lack is the shared understanding that comes from a stable group.
choices: a temporary space that offers comfort but no sense of belonging
a room that has been decorated far more expensively than necessary
a place where students prepare for examinations in complete quiet
an area that colleges use only when dormitories are being repaired
a lounge that residents share with many other unfamiliar students
implication.explanation_ko: '잘 갖춰진 대기실'이라는 비유는 편의는 충분하지만 소속감은 주지 못한 채 기다리기만 하는 임시 공간이라는 뜻이다. ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②과도한 장식, ③시험 준비 공간, ④보수 기간 대체 공간, ⑤공용 라운지는 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: The most fundamental cognitive motivation encourages people to understand their environment.
Most important, people prefer to develop meanings that are shared with other people.
When a college admits more students than it expects, some end up living in campus hotels.
It is easy to understand why living in a lounge is problematic, for it offers no closet.
After all, students in a hotel gets private bathrooms, their own television and larger rooms.
Nevertheless, those residents are not part of a stable group of year-long neighbors.
They lack a shared social understanding, normally developed from membership in a stable group.
grammar.explanation_ko: ④ 주어는 복수 students이고 in a hotel은 수식어구이므로 동사는 get이어야 한다. gets는 수 일치 오류이다. ④가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①encourage + to V, ②선행사 meanings를 받는 주격 that, ③end up -ing의 동명사 living, ⑤수동 관계의 과거분사 developed는 모두 옳다.

passage: The most fundamental cognitive motivation encourages people to predict what will happen in case of uncertainties.
Most important, people prefer to develop meanings that are shared with other people.
When a college admits more students than expected, some end up living in dorm lounges or campus hotels.
It is easy to understand why living in a lounge is problematic, since it offers no closet.
After all, students in a hotel get private bathrooms, their own television and larger rooms.
Nevertheless, those residents are not part of a temporary group of year-long neighbors.
They lack a shared social understanding, normally developed from membership in a stable group.
vocab.explanation_ko: ④ 호텔 거주자에게 없는 것은 1년 내내 이웃이 되어 줄 '안정된(stable)' 집단이다. temporary(일시적인)는 정반대이므로 stable로 고쳐야 한다. ④가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①uncertainties(불확실성), ②shared(공유된), ③problematic(문제가 있는), ⑤membership(소속)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: The most basic cognitive motivation drives people to make sense of their surroundings and predict events.

choices: a clear plan for their future career
blank.explanation_ko: 호텔은 편의를 모두 갖췄지만 1년간 이웃이 될 안정된 집단이 없다. 따라서 결여된 것은 그 집단에서 형성되는 '공유된 사회적 이해'이다. ④가 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①조용한 공부 공간, ②수납 공간, ③행정 서비스 접근성, ⑤진로 계획은 호텔이 이미 갖췄거나 본문에 근거가 없다.

sentences: Above all, people prefer to develop meanings that other people around them share as well.
When a college admits more students than expected, some of them end up living in dorm lounges or campus hotels.

Universities with larger endowments generally spend more money on athletic facilities than on classroom buildings.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '공유된 사회적 이해와 안정된 집단의 필요'를 다루는데 ④ '대학 기금 규모와 체육 시설 지출'은 전혀 다른 주제로 흐름을 끊는 무관한 문장이다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②③⑤는 모두 공유된 의미의 필요와 호텔·라운지 사례로 자연스럽게 이어진다.

order.given: Of the cognitive motivations, the most fundamental one pushes people to understand their environment so that they can predict what is coming.

blocks.A: The lounge is easy to criticize, since it has no closet, but a campus hotel room comes with a private bathroom, a personal television and more space.
blocks.B: Most important, people prefer meanings that other people share, which is why an over-enrolled college creates a revealing situation when it houses students in lounges and campus hotels.
blocks.C: Nevertheless, the hotel residents are the ones who suffer, for they belong to no stable group and must wait in uncertainty, lacking the shared social understanding a settled group provides.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 인지 동기를 (B)가 '공유되는 의미'로 좁히며 사례를 도입하고, (A)가 라운지와 호텔을 비교하며, (C)가 Nevertheless로 반전 결론을 낸다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (A)는 (B)가 제시한 사례를 전제로 하므로 먼저 올 수 없고, (C)의 Nevertheless는 (A)의 호텔 장점을 받아야 성립한다.

insert.insert_sentence: After all, students in a hotel get private bathrooms, their own TV, and larger rooms.

passage_marked.text: Most important, people prefer to develop meanings that are shared with other people.
For example, if more people accept offers of admission than a college expects, quite a few students end up living in dorm lounges or campus hotels.
It is easy to understand why living in the lounge is problematic, for it offers no closet.
But what is wrong with a room at campus hotels?

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 After all은 '호텔 방에 무슨 문제가 있는가'라는 의문에 대한 상식적 근거를 덧붙이는 말이므로 그 질문 바로 뒤, 그리고 In fact로 시작하는 반전 앞에 와야 한다. ④가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장이 없으면 In fact가 뒤집을 통념(호텔이 더 좋다)이 제시되지 않아 논리가 성립하지 않는다.

passage: People are driven above all to understand their surroundings well enough to predict them.
For this reason they prefer meanings that the people around them also hold.
An over-enrolled college may house extra students in lounges or in campus hotels.
The lounge lacks a closet and any real privacy, so its problems are obvious.
The hotel room provides a private bathroom, a personal television and more space.
Yet hotel residents belong to no settled circle of neighbors for the year.
They must wait in uncertainty until they find a social place of their own.
The uncertainty, rather than the room itself, is what troubles them.
summary.summary_template: Students in comfortable hotel rooms feel worse than those in bare lounges because material __(A)__ cannot replace the shared understanding that comes from __(B)__ to a stable group.
summary.explanation_ko: 물질적 (A)comfort(편안함)로는 안정된 집단에 (B)belonging(속함)에서 나오는 공유된 이해를 대체할 수 없다. ②가 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 hardship이나 isolation이 아니라 comfort이고, (B)는 objecting·listening·returning이 아니라 belonging이어야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.answer: The uncertainty itself is the problem.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 The uncertainty + 강조의 재귀대명사 itself + is the problem.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 사람들은 다른 사람들과 공유되는 의미를 형성하기를 선호한다.
writing.answer: People prefer to develop meanings that are shared with other people.
writing.explanation_ko: prefer to V + 선행사 meanings를 수식하는 주격 관계절 that are shared.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그 학생들은 자신의 사회적 자리를 찾기 전에 불확실한 상태로 기다려야 한다.
writing.answer: They must wait in uncertainty before finding their social niche.
writing.explanation_ko: must + 동사원형 wait, before + 동명사 finding 구조.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: People lack a shared social understanding, normally developed from membership in a ___________ group.
writing.explanation_ko: 공유된 사회적 이해는 '안정된(stable)' 집단의 소속에서 형성된다.

writing.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Although campus hotel rooms offer greater (A)___________, their residents suffer because they have no (B)___________ group that would give them a shared social understanding.
writing.explanation_ko: 호텔은 더 큰 편안함(comfort)을 주지만 안정된(stable) 집단이 없어 공유된 이해를 얻지 못한다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: In fact, living in those hotels is problematic because the student residents are not a part of a stable group with people who will be their neighbors for the year.
writing.answer: 실제로 그 호텔에서 사는 것이 문제인 이유는 그 학생 거주자들이 그해 동안 자신의 이웃이 될 사람들과 함께하는 안정된 집단의 일부가 아니기 때문이다.
writing.explanation_ko: because절의 이유, people을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 who에 유의한다.
